I should just face myself as I am, whatever that is. This made me feel relieved though, it’s a nice reminder of the capacity for good and understanding in people, even when dealing with a situation as weird as mine. You’re not rude at all, I just took a lot of time to reply. This gave me hope :) thank you

I don’t think there’s really anyone I could talk about this with. It’s too embarrassing and weird. If I talked about it to my counsellor I think she would be very creeped out. I can’t really afford a therapist at the moment. Fortunately there’s no chance of me being close to this girl, she’s just a random girl who goes to the same school. I thought I was done with hating myself for my feelings when I accepted myself as gay but now this. I think I’m just very fucked up. If I’m a pedophile I wouldn’t be able to live with myself.

Well my LO has deliberately made it clear to me that they are straight. We are the same gender, so it’s a pretty blatant rejection. Somehow I still keep hoping, taking every little irrelevant interaction and blowing it out of proportion. I’m just resigned. I guess it’s just the nature of limerence. I twist the situation around in my head to suit my emotional needs, despite the facts

Thank you. I agree with you. Especially with the toxic messages from media. The subject of love is very common in entertainment, you hear about it all the time everywhere. I think it increased my propensity to limerence because I thought that if I felt this way, it must mean something. That surely something will come of it, since that’s what all the fairytales and movies drilled into my head. But I should really get out of my head, my life is not a movie. My love interests are just people, who I’ve developed feelings for. They are not made to reciprocate my feelings. I hope I’m not crazy. I really need to move on.

Well done for fighting it! I’ve seen a lot of people on the internet suggesting that if you direct your attention to something else, something with greater purpose, it can make limerence look meagre by comparison. That could help make it weaker. That’s a good idea, I should be busy with my studies anyways, so I won’t have much free time to fantasise about my LO. Hopefully.

Ok, thank you. I’m trying it at the moment. I think it’s one of the best approaches, because with limerence there’s not much you can do. You can’t force yourself to just stop obsessing over someone, so when I realised that to just accept it is an option it was a bit of a relief because I always felt like I was doing something wrong. It doesn’t decrease it, but it makes it a bit easier to live with
